title: Latency posture — weekly brief and handoff (Apr 09 2029)
body:
Summary

This week we saw two short-lived latency regressions related to embeddings inference and routing fallbacks. Overall customer-facing P95 stayed within the SLO but P99 spikes were noticeable during traffic bursts. Notes below include timeline, preliminary root-cause hypotheses, immediate mitigations, and outstanding follow-ups for the next on-call rotation.

Incident highlights (short form)
- 2029-04-06 03:12 UTC — Embedding cache thrash: transient P99 spike (~850 ms -> 1.4 s) for ~40 minutes affecting hosted-api region-eu-west-1. Error rate did not increase. On-call: Marcus C.
  - Symptom: sudden increase in cold cache misses and concurrent KV eviction churn. PVC metrics showed elevated IO wait on node-group-g2.
  - Immediate mitigation: disabled autoscale burst on pool-eu-g2 (reduced new allocations) + increased soft cache TTL on embedding-prefix. Latency recovered in ~18 minutes after lowering allocation pressure.
  - Follow-ups: deeper KV cache eviction profiling (Ethan P), evaluate moving hot-prefix to reserved shard (Lina G). JIRA: SRE-4123.

- 2029-04-08 15:40 UTC — Smart-routing fallback loop: brief P95/P99 increase (~300 ms -> 900 ms) for <10 minutes when region fallback policy triggered between model-v1-small and model-v2-quant. On-call: Aisha P.
  - Symptom: two pools reported near-capacity and the router decided to fallback to cross-region routes; repeated re-routing events caused extra serialization overhead.
  - Immediate mitigation: force pinned route to model-v1-small for enterprise-tier customers while autoscaling completed. Observed no customer errors.
  - Follow-ups: add hysteresis to router decisions to avoid oscillation (SRE-4187), simulate fallback under heavy traffic in staging.

SLO & metrics snapshot (weekly)
- P50: 35 ms (steady)
- P95: 210 ms (target 250 ms)
- P99: 820 ms (target 700 ms) — slight exceedance during bursts this week
- Error budget consumed (monthly window): 6.8% used (target < 10%)
- Notes: P99 is the area of concern; main contributors are cold cache misses and routing-induced CPU stalls.

Runbook / Playbook updates
- Embedding cache runbook: added a new checklist for safe TTL bump and a command set to drain/reserve hot prefixes without taking the pool offline. Draft changes in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/284. Owner: Ethan P.
- Router hysteresis doc: initial design notes in confluence:Latency-Posture-Playbook. Propose 30s decision window with exponential backoff for repeated fallback flips. Owner: Lina G.

On-call handoff (what incoming on-call needs to know)
- Active items to monitor (next 48h):
  - Embedding cache eviction rate and KV IO wait on node-group-g2 (alert: kv-evict-rate > 500/s sustained 5m). Owner: Ethan P.
  - Router fallback oscillation counter and recent route-change history (alert: route-flip > 3 in 2m). Owner: Lina G.
  - Autoscaler throttles log: check for queued allocation failures during spikes. Owner: Platform-eng duty.
- Access notes: to investigate cache tiering, you'll need access to cluster-monitoring (kube context: eu-g2-prod) and the kv-inspector tool (internal CLI).
- Escalation path: if P99 > 1.5s for >10m, escalate to SRE lead (Marcus Chen) and call platform-engineering for emergency reserved-shard allocation.

Action items and owners (short tickler)
- Ethan P: run a 50k requests/min cache churn sim in staging, produce heatmap of eviction hotspots (due 2029-04-16).
- Lina G: implement router hysteresis PoC and add route-flip metric (due 2029-04-19).
- Marcus C: review autoscaler logs & suggest tuning to avoid simultaneous large allocations (due 2029-04-15).
- Aisha P: update incident blameless writeup and prep postmortem draft for SRE review (due 2029-04-14).

Notes to self / rough ideas (brainstorm)
- Consider a lightweight local hot-shard for embeddings pinned at the request router level for the top ~10% prefixes (cheap mem, big impact on P99).
- Evaluate opportunistic pre-warm on observed daily peaks (predictive pre-warm policy). Might be a good Optimize feature.
- Could we add a short-lived, lower-cost quantized model variant that gets routed during fallback to reduce CPU serialization?

Outstanding questions
- Why did node-group-g2 show IO wait specifically during Monday morning traffic ramp? Hypothesis: competing infra jobs (backups) overlapped; need infra schedule correlation.
- Does the autoscaler consider soft cache TTL when deciding pool capacity? If not, we should pass cache pressure signals into scaling heuristics.

Meeting notes (mini transcript from 2029-04-09 ops sync)
- Marcus: "We saw embedding eviction spike at 03:12, cache TTL bump helped but we need to instrument eviction reasons."
- Lina: "Router flip was noisy; hysteresis should be a simple delta with time window."
- Ethan: "I'll add per-prefix hit-rate heatmaps — that should show hot-prefix concentration and make a reserved shard easy."
- Action: plan a 1-hr runbook drill next Tuesday to rehearse cache TTL bump and reserved shard failover.

Links / quick refs
- JIRA: SRE-4123 (embedding-cache-thrash)
- JIRA: SRE-4187 (routing-hysteresis)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/284
- Confluence playbook: confluence:Latency-Posture-Playbook

If you're taking the handoff: read the embedding-cache checklist first, then watch last 2 hours of metrics (grafana: "embeddings/cache-evictions-eu-g2"), then glance at router-flip count dashboard.

-- Aisha
